components.note: 北 (north; two people back to back) — in older Chinese 乖 meant 'at odds, contrary' (乖张), which fits two figures turned away; 'well-behaved' is the later colloquial sense.
千 (thousand) — sits on top. Memory aid: no reliable etymology; picture a child with a thousand reasons to misbehave who still stays put.
方 (square; flag) — stands in for the flag part 㫃 of the old form, as in 旗 flag, 旅 travel, 族 clan; the meaning 'bestow, carry out' came later.
㐌 (looks like 也 plus a stroke) — traditionally the sound part (也 yě); today the match with shī is only a loose clue.
韦 (leather; from 韋) — the right half. 韩 is mainly a name today (Korea, surname Han); the parts no longer explain the meaning.
龺 (sunrays over a pole) — the left part, the same as in 乾 and 朝. Memory aid: just a visual block; say 'hán' by its look, not by its parts.
夫 (man) is written twice, side by side — one man standing in for another, i.e. 'to replace, on behalf of' (替我 for me).
日 (sun) — the dictionary calls it a sound part, but tì ≠ rì, so treat that as unproven. Memory aid: two men take turns under the sun.
雨 (rain) — the top part. Not about weather here: 霸 first meant pale moonlight and was later borrowed for 'tyrant, overlord' (霸道, 称霸).
革 (leather, to reform) and 月 (moon/flesh) form the lower part. Memory aid: an overlord rules above the rain, with leather armour (革) and the moon (月) beneath.
之 (to go; foot stepping on) — the dictionary reads 乏 as a foot 之 blocked by a stroke 丿: unable to move on, so 'lacking, tired' (缺乏, 疲乏).
丿 (a left-falling stroke) — the blocking stroke on top. Memory aid: a barrier cutting across the road, so you run short.
去 (to go) — 丢 looks like 去 with an extra stroke on top. Memory aid: something that 'goes' away is lost.
厶 (private, small) — the lower part, as in 去. The dictionary story (a lost piece of jade 玉) is a later reading, not proven.
氺 (water, a variant of 水) — the old form has water below hands and a big person above: calm, great, secure. Same character in 泰国 Thailand.
大 (big) — top of the character. Memory aid: a big (大) volume of water held steady is calm and 'great'.
亏 is the simplified form of 虧, whose 虍 (tiger) part was dropped; the leftover shape no longer shows the meaning. Memory aid: it looks like 于 with a hook — 'cut short, a loss'.
人 (person) — the roof-like top. 余 absorbed 餘 (food left over); the shape no longer explains 'remainder'. Memory aid: a person with leftovers.
食 (food) — the old 餘 had the food part 饣; 余 is its sound part (yú), the same series as 除 chú, 徐 xú, 途 tú, with loose matches.
彐 (broom top, from 帚) — in the old form 歸 a woman with a broom 帚 'returns' to her husband's home; the story is a traditional account, not proven.
追 (zhuī) — the old form 歸 is said to use 追-like parts for sound; guī is only a loose match. Treat as a memory aid, not a rule.
宀 (roof, house) — a house family: 家 home, 安 safe, 室 room. 奥 originally meant the inner, dark corner of a house, hence 'mysterious, profound'.
米 (rice) — in the middle; the dictionary's story is a person finding a house full of rice. Memory aid, not proven.
大 (big) — the bottom. Memory aid: something big and hidden deep inside the house is mysterious.
匸 (a hiding box, open at the side) — the frame around 儿. Rare radical, not meaningful on its own.
儿 (legs) — the legs below. Memory aid: 匹 counts horses (一匹马) — think of a horse's legs under a covering, or a bolt of cloth rolled up.
艹 (grass, plants) — the plant radical, as in 花 flower, 草 grass. In 萨 it no longer carries meaning; 萨 only appears in transliterations such as 菩萨 bodhisattva.
产 (to produce) — the lower right part. Memory aid: sound-only character; learn it as a unit from 菩萨, 萨克斯.
尸 (body, shelter) — often a building or cover: 屋 house, 层 storey, 居 dwell. In 屉 it suggests a shelter, such as a drawer or tray in a case.
世 (shì) — probably a loose sound clue for tì, but not certain. Memory aid: a drawer (抽屉) is a tier that slides in and out of a world of its own.
勹 (to wrap) — wraps around 厶, like a hook curling round something. Memory aid, not a proven origin.
厶 (small, private) — the tucked-in part. 勾 is the sound part of 沟 gōu ditch, 钩 gōu hook, 构 gòu build, with hook-like meaning in 勾引.
鱼 (fish) — the old 魯 had fish on top; the meaning 'foolish, rash' is later and not about fish. 鲁 is mostly the state and surname Lu.
日 (sun) — at the bottom (from older 白). Memory aid: a fish gaping in the sun is dazed — hence foolish, rash.
用 (to use) — 甩 looks like 用 with the last stroke flicked out. Memory aid: use something up by flinging it away.
白 (white) — the top. 皂 means soap but also black (皂白 = black and white, as in 不分皂白). Memory aid: soap makes things 白 white.
七 (seven) — the bottom, probably a changed older shape. Memory aid only: seven bars of soap. The true origin is unclear.
幺 (tiny thread) — the dictionary story is a cord pulled taut in a frame, so 'to lead'; another account sees a bird net. Origin is disputed.
十 (ten) — the lower bar. Reads shuài to lead (率领) and lǜ for rate (效率, 比率). Memory aid: ten threads pulled together as a rate.
彳 (step, walk) — the road family: 行 go, 往 toward. 徽 originally meant a cord; the 'emblem, badge' sense is a later extension (徽章).
糸 (silk thread; here 系) — the old meaning is a rope. 徽 looks like 微 (wēi) with a thread added; the sound link to huī is only loose.
爫 (hand, claw) — a hand pressing down; the traditional account is a hand calming a woman, so 'settled, secure'. Treat as a memory aid.
女 (woman) — a family also in 好 good, 妈 mum, 姓 surname; here the person being settled. Used in 妥当 proper, 妥协 compromise.
几 (low table) — the dictionary reads the shape as a plate or stand. Origin of 凡 'all, ordinary' is debated.
丶 (dot) — a small mark inside. 凡 is the sound part of 帆 fān sail and 矾 fán alum; also in 平凡 ordinary. Memory aid: a dot on a plain table.
子 (child) — on the left. 孔 means a hole or opening; 孔子 is Confucius, whose surname is 孔.
乚 (a hook) — the dictionary story is a baby's mouth, unproven. Memory aid: a child with a hook-shaped opening, a small hole.
目 (eye) — the top part is a stacked eye 罒; 睾 is a variant of 睪, the part in 译 yì, 泽 zé, 择 zé, 释 shì; sound clue is loose and the meaning sense is modern.
幸 (luck) — the lower part, with no useful meaning link. Only used in 睾丸; learn it as a fixed word.
虍 (tiger stripes) — the tiger family: 虎 tiger, 虚 empty, 处 place. A tiger awe may suggest 'devout', but that is a guess.
文 (writing, culture) — the lower part. Memory aid: devout people honour ritual and writing (文) with the awe one has for a tiger.
而 (and; an old picture of a beard) — the top part. The dictionary story is a woman in a false beard having fun (play-acting); a memory aid.
女 (woman) — the bottom. Used in 耍赖 act shamelessly, 玩耍 to play, 耍帅 to show off.
艹 (grass) — on top, but in 若 it is most likely a worn-down picture of hair, not plants; oracle forms show a person smoothing hair, meaning 'to yield'.
右 (right hand) — below. 若 is the sound part of 诺 nuò promise and 惹 rě, loosely; used for 'if' (若是), 'like' (若无其事).
几 (low table) — what you lean on. 凭 means to lean on, so to rely on (凭证 proof, 凭什么 on what basis).
任 (to trust, to bear) — the top part. The dictionary story is leaning on a table; its sound does not match píng. Memory aid: lean on something you trust.
齐 is the simplified form of 齊, a picture of ears of grain growing evenly level — hence 'even, together, complete'. Sound clue: 剂 jì, 挤 jǐ, 济 jì.
文 (writing) — the visible top part in the simplified form, not the meaning. Memory aid: neat writing in even lines is 整齐.
幺 (tiny thread) twice — the lower part. 兹 is the sound part of 滋 zī, 慈 cí and 磁 cí; the meaning (now, this) is a borrowing.
艹 (grass-like top) — in the old form 茲 it is a grass cover, but it no longer means plants in this character. Mostly used in 兹 'herewith'.
八 (eight; to divide) — breath dispersing to both sides. 兮 is an old poetic particle, 'ah!', as in the Chu Ci poems.
丂 (breath bending against an obstacle) — also in 考 test and 巧 clever, where it gives a sound hint (kǎo, qiǎo). Together: breath flowing out, a sigh.
彳 (step, walk) — the road family: 行 go, 往 toward. 後 is the traditional form of 后 'after, behind' (之后 after); 彳 shows the walking.
幺 (thread) and 夂 (a foot dragging) — a thread tied to the foot makes you lag behind: 'after, behind'. The accepted account, not a sound hint.
夂 (foot coming down slowly) — the lower foot, as in 冬 winter, 处 place, 夏 summer. In 後 it means being slow, trailing.
户 (door) — the door family: 房 room, 所 place. 扁 was the inscribed board hung over a door, hence 'sign, plaque', then 'flat' (扁平).
册 (bound strips, a book) — what is written on the board. 扁 is also the sound part of 编 biān, 偏 piān, 篇 piān, 遍 biàn, 骗 piàn.
厂 (cliff) — a family: 厚 thick, 原 origin, 压 press. In 厄 it is the heavy overhang pressing down.
㔾 (a kneeling person, also written 卩) — the person under the cliff: crushed, in distress. 厄 means hardship, as in 厄运 bad luck.
巾 (cloth) — hanging below the 口. Memory aid: a cloth dangling from a loop, so 'to hang' (吊灯 hanging lamp). The 'condole' sense (吊唁) is separate.
口 (mouth, opening) — the top. It may be only a loop or hook here; not a meaning clue. No settled etymology; treat the picture as a memory aid.
大 (big) — the top. 奈 comes from 柰 (a crabapple 木 + 示); the sense 'how, to endure' is borrowed, as in 无奈 helpless, 奈何 what can be done.
示 (altar, to show) — the bottom; its 礻 form is in 神 spirit, 礼 ritual. Here it is just the visible part; the meaning is borrowed from the sound.
色 (colour, beauty) — the colour part; 艳 means vividly beautiful: 艳丽 gorgeous, 鲜艳 bright. The traditional form is 艷.
丰 (abundant) — the left part: a rich, full look. Together: richly colourful, glamorous.
比 (side by side, to compare) — two people next to each other, as in 比较. The top part of 皆: 'all, together'.
白 (white) — the bottom; here probably a worn form of an older shape (自 'each'), not 'white'. Memory aid: everyone lined up in a row — all of them.
厂 (cliff) — a family: 原 origin, 压 press, 厅 hall. 厚 originally meant a thick mound or hill, hence 'thick, deep' (厚度 thickness).
日 (sun) — together with 子 (child) in the inner part. Dictionary story: sunlight and children in a house; a memory aid, not proven.
尸 (body, shelter) — the top part, as in 层 storey, 居 dwell. 届 is 屆 simplified, meaning 'to arrive', then a term of office (本届).
由 (from, by) — the lower part, standing in for the old shape. The sound yóu does not match jiè, so do not use it as a sound hint.
⺊ (a divining crack, from 卜) — the top. 卢 is simplified from 盧 (a cooking vessel); the shapes no longer show it. Mostly used as a surname.
尸 (shelter) — below. 卢 is the sound part of 炉 lú stove, 芦 lú reed, 庐 lú hut, 颅 lú skull; also in 驴 lǘ donkey, with a loose match.
寸 (inch; hand) — the lower part, also in 对 and 导. 寿 comes from 壽, an old form of 老 (old) with a sound part; it means long life.
丰 (abundant) — the upper part. Memory aid: abundant years under a careful hand. Sound clue: 寿 appears in 涛 tāo and 筹 chóu loosely.
羊 (sheep) — the top. 姜 is the Jiang clan name; the 'ginger' meaning (生姜) is borrowed from the old 薑. Memory aid: sheep and ginger go well together.
女 (woman) — many ancient clan names carry it: 姓 surname, 姬, 姚. Here it marks 姜 as a clan name, not female meaning.
氏 is a plain unit; the dictionary reads it as a person bowing down, but its origin is debated. Meaning: clan or family name, as in 姓氏, 氏族, 摄氏 Celsius.
衣 (clothes) — a family: 表 outside, 袋 bag, 装 dress. 裔 first meant the hem of a robe; far from the body, hence far descendants (后裔).
冏 (window; bright) — the lower part; the dictionary calls it a meaning part. Memory aid: the hem trails down, like descendants far from the ancestors.
且 (moreover; once an altar) — the top part. 县 is simplified from 縣, which meant 'to hang'; counties were said to hang directly from the ruler. Origin: traditional account.
厶 (small, private) — the bottom. 县 is also the base of 悬 xuán, 'to hang' (悬挂), which adds a heart 心.
方 (square; flag) — the left part; here it is part of a worn picture, not the direction. 於 means 'at, in, to' (as 于), and is also a surname.
乌 (crow) — 於 is generally traced to a crow picture, whose sound was borrowed for the preposition. Origin: traditional account.
亦 is an old picture of a person (大) with two dots marking the armpits — the original word for armpit. 'Also' is a sound borrowing; 腋 yè later took over armpit.
亠 (lid) — the visible top. Sound clue: 亦 is the sound part of 弈 yì chess, 奕 yì, 迹 jì trace.
